creator: Marc Lou

one_line: Bubble builds the product. Unlock SaaS finds the customer for the product Bubble built. Sequential, not interchangeable.
what_it_is: A visual builder for full web applications without code|A way for non-engineers to ship a real product with a database and logic|A common way the Unlock SaaS audience shipped their first version
what_it_is_not: A way to get someone to pay for what you built|A diagnostic of why your app is converting at zero|A guarantee tied to your Stripe ledger
who_for_it: Non-engineers who want to build a functional web app with data and workflows without writing code.
who_not_for_it: Founders who already built their app on Bubble and still have no paying customers.
honest_verdict: Bubble solved the build-the-app problem for non-engineers. The next problem, finding a customer, is a different problem, and Bubble never claimed to solve it. Unlock SaaS is built for the Bubble-shaped founder: shipped a real product, now staring at a flat Stripe line and needing the marketing-and-sales playbook that the builder does not provide.
pricing_note: Bubble has a free tier and paid subscription plans. Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Zapier, Inc.
one_line: Zapier connects your tools. Unlock SaaS connects your product to a customer. Different kinds of plumbing.
what_it_is: A no-code automation platform that moves data between apps|A way to wire up the operational plumbing of a SaaS|A time-saver for repetitive multi-tool workflows
what_it_is_not: A customer-acquisition playbook|A diagnosis of why your offer is not selling|A guarantee that shipping will produce a paying customer
who_for_it: Founders who need to connect their stack, move data between tools, or automate repetitive operational steps.
who_not_for_it: Founders whose stack is already connected but who still have no paying customers.
honest_verdict: Zapier is genuinely useful for operating a business once you have one. It does not answer the question of why nobody is paying yet. The two tools rarely compete: you use Zapier to run the machinery and Unlock SaaS to fill the pipeline that feeds it.
pricing_note: Zapier has a free tier and paid plans based on task volume. Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Sam Ovens
one_line: Skool hosts a community. Unlock SaaS runs the playbook that gets you customers to put in one. Different layers.
what_it_is: A flat-fee platform for running a paid community and courses|A place to host members, lessons, and discussion in one product|A growing home for creator-led cohorts and masterminds
what_it_is_not: A SaaS launch curriculum|A diagnostic of why your product page converts at zero|A mechanism that verifies your Stripe revenue and refunds you if nothing sells
who_for_it: Creators and educators who want a simple, all-in-one place to host a paid community or course.
who_not_for_it: Non-engineer SaaS founders who already shipped a product and need customers for it, not a place to host a community.
honest_verdict: Skool is excellent at its job: hosting a community. Its job is not to get you your first SaaS customer, which is why the two products sit on different layers. Many Unlock SaaS members run a Skool community later, once they have an audience; the Playbook is for the earlier step, when there is no audience yet.
pricing_note: Skool is a flat-rate platform at approximately $99/month per group (verified 2026-08-13). Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Gumroad, Inc.
one_line: Gumroad sells digital products. Unlock SaaS gets you a SaaS customer. Different products, different checkout.
what_it_is: A fast checkout for digital products, courses, and memberships|A low-friction way for creators to sell without building a store|A platform optimized for one-off digital-product sales
what_it_is_not: A SaaS launch curriculum|A diagnosis of why your subscription product is not selling|A refund tied to your Stripe ledger as a performance guarantee
who_for_it: Creators selling ebooks, courses, templates, or other digital products directly to an audience.
who_not_for_it: Founders selling a recurring SaaS subscription who need their first paying customer and a repeatable acquisition playbook.
honest_verdict: Gumroad is the right tool for selling a digital product to an audience that already exists. Unlock SaaS is for the earlier, harder problem: building the offer and the acquisition motion so a recurring SaaS product has its first customer. They are complementary: sell a template on Gumroad, sell the SaaS with the Playbook.
pricing_note: Gumroad is free to use and charges a flat fee per sale (10% as of 2026-08-13). Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Alex Iliescu (Strategic Flow Tech, Tenerife, Spain)
one_line: Strategic Flow rebuilds the email itself. Unlock SaaS finds the customers who receive it. Different problems, complementary tools.
what_it_is: A diagnostic service that scores a single SaaS email 1-10 against a 7-point Decision Friction Model|A same-day rebuild of that email: diagnosis, rebuilt version, and 3 A/B subject line variants|A 59-teardown public archive of named B2B SaaS emails (Semrush, HeyGen, Optimizely, Revolut, Wrike, Zoho) with scores and fixes
what_it_is_not: A deliverability tool: it does not fix bounce rates, spam placement, or sender reputation|A lifecycle or automation audit: it diagnoses the individual message, not the flows around it|A customer-acquisition playbook tied to your Stripe ledger
who_for_it: B2B SaaS founders and marketing managers whose open rates are acceptable (above 20%) but click rates are not (below 2%), and newsletter operators with 1,000+ subscribers.
who_not_for_it: Founders who have not yet sent the emails or built the audience: the audit is only worth it once messages are going out and getting opened but not clicked.
honest_verdict: Strategic Flow is a sharp, narrowly-scoped diagnostic: it names the structural reason a specific email fails to convert after it is opened. The problem it does not touch is the one before it: who the email goes to, how many send, and whether the offer behind it can convert at all. That is Unlock SaaS territory. The natural sequence is the reverse of what most founders expect: build the demand and offer layer with Unlock SaaS first, then sharpen each individual send with a Strategic Flow teardown.
pricing_note: Strategic Flow has a $49 one-time Diagnostic Audit, a $499 one-time Full Architecture Rebuild, and monthly plans; no subscription required to start (verified 2026-08-15). Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Wix.com Ltd.
one_line: Wix builds the site. Unlock SaaS finds the customers who visit it. Different jobs, different tools.
what_it_is: A drag-and-drop website builder with hosting and a large template library|A way for a non-technical founder to publish a polished site fast|A platform that bundles domains, hosting, and design in one place
what_it_is_not: A diagnosis of why a live site still converts at zero|A customer-acquisition playbook tied to your Stripe ledger|A sales-and-outreach motion that runs after the site is live
who_for_it: Founders who need a professional website or landing page and want to build it themselves without writing code.
who_not_for_it: Founders whose site is already live and polished but still has no paying customers.
honest_verdict: Wix is very good at the problem it solves: turning a non-technical founder into someone with a clean, live website in an afternoon. The problem it does not touch is the one most post-launch founders actually have, which is that the site exists, looks fine, and still nobody buys. Unlock SaaS treats that disease directly. The two are commonly used in sequence: build the page on Wix, then run the customer-acquisition playbook on the offer that page presents.
pricing_note: Wix has a free plan and paid site plans that start around $17/month (verified 2026-08-14). Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Shopify Inc.
one_line: Shopify builds the store. Unlock SaaS finds the customers for what the store sells. Different layers.
what_it_is: A hosted platform for building and running an online store|A payments, inventory, and checkout system in one product|A fast way for a founder to sell physical or digital products online
what_it_is_not: A way to get someone to pay for what the store sells|A diagnosis of why a product page has no buyers|A refund tied to your Stripe ledger as a performance guarantee
who_for_it: Founders selling products who want a reliable, hosted store with payments and inventory handled for them.
who_not_for_it: Founders who already have a store and a product but still have no customers.
honest_verdict: Shopify is the default answer for selling products online, and it earns that position. What it does not do is make anyone buy. A store that is live on Shopify and converting at zero has a demand or offer problem, not a platform problem. Unlock SaaS is aimed at the SaaS-shaped version of that problem, but the underlying logic is the same: shipping the store is not the same as getting the first paying customer.
pricing_note: Shopify starts around $39/month on its Basic plan plus transaction fees, with a free trial (verified 2026-08-14). Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Intuit Inc.
one_line: Mailchimp sends email to a list. Unlock SaaS helps you build the offer that gets a list worth emailing.
what_it_is: An email marketing platform for campaigns, automations, and lists|A way to design and send newsletters and drip sequences|A tool for managing subscribers and tracking email engagement
what_it_is_not: A way to get the first customer who reads the email|A diagnosis of why your offer is not converting|A mechanism that verifies your Stripe revenue and refunds you if nothing sells
who_for_it: Founders who already have an audience or list and need to communicate with it regularly.
who_not_for_it: Founders who have no list and no customers yet, and need the offer and acquisition motion first.
honest_verdict: Mailchimp is excellent at the problem it solves: sending reliable, well-designed email to a list that already exists. The problem it does not solve is acquiring the customer who should be on that list in the first place. Unlock SaaS targets the earlier step. A founder who has shipped a product and has nobody to email does not need a better email tool; they need a playbook for the first paying customer.
pricing_note: Mailchimp has a free tier and paid plans that scale with contact count. Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: beehiiv Inc.
one_line: beehiiv grows a newsletter. Unlock SaaS gets a SaaS product its first customer. Different businesses.
what_it_is: A platform for writing, growing, and monetising a newsletter|A growth engine for audience-led media businesses|A way to run a paid or free email publication
what_it_is_not: A SaaS launch curriculum|A diagnosis of why a product is not selling|A refund tied to your Stripe ledger
who_for_it: Writers and creators building a newsletter or media audience, especially those monetising through subscriptions.
who_not_for_it: SaaS founders who shipped a product and need their first paying customer, not a publication.
honest_verdict: beehiiv is the right tool for building an audience-first media business, and it is very good at that. It is not a tool for getting a SaaS product its first customer, and it never claims to be. The two can coexist for the same founder: build the newsletter on beehiiv once there is an audience, and use Unlock SaaS for the earlier, harder step of getting a product that people will pay for.
pricing_note: beehiiv has a free tier and paid plans starting around $39/month for the Scale plan (verified 2026-08-14). Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.

creator: Kajabi LLC
one_line: Kajabi sells courses and memberships. Unlock SaaS gets a SaaS product its first customer. Different offers.
what_it_is: An all-in-one platform for selling courses, coaching, and memberships|A way for creators to run a knowledge business with marketing funnels built in|A product for turning expertise into a paid offering
what_it_is_not: A SaaS launch curriculum|A diagnosis of why your product page converts at zero|A mechanism that verifies Stripe revenue and refunds you if nothing sells
who_for_it: Creators and educators selling courses, coaching, or memberships and wanting the funnel tooling bundled in.
who_not_for_it: SaaS founders who shipped a product and need customers for it, not a platform for selling expertise.
honest_verdict: Kajabi is a serious, well-built platform for the creator economy, and its price reflects that it bundles a lot of funnel machinery. It is the wrong shape for a SaaS founder whose problem is a flat Stripe line: that founder does not need another course platform, they need an honest diagnosis of why the product is not selling and a playbook to fix it. Unlock SaaS is aimed squarely at that second person.
pricing_note: Kajabi is a paid platform starting around $149/month with no free tier (verified 2026-08-14). Unlock SaaS is $1 Starter + $49/month Playbook.
